title: Meet Josh Heuston: The Sri Lankan-Australian Star Quietly Conquering Every Streaming Platform
excerpt: From Heartbreak High to Dune: Prophecy to Prime Video's Off Campus — the Baulkham Hills actor is building a filmography that NRIs should know about.
body:
When Prime Video dropped Off Campus on May 13, the internet mostly talked about the ice hockey romance, the Elle Kennedy source material, and the sizzling chemistry between leads Ella Bright and Belmont Cameli. But for anyone paying attention to the ensemble, one name kept surfacing in a different kind of conversation: Josh Heuston — the 29-year-old Australian actor of Anglo-Sri Lankan descent who plays Justin Kohl, the band's brooding musician with a complicated romantic arc.

Heuston isn't new to the streaming world. He broke out as the impossibly cool Dusty Reid in Netflix's Heartbreak High reboot, a role he carried across three seasons from 2022 to 2026. Then came the prestige callback: Constantine Corrino in HBO's Dune: Prophecy, planting him squarely in the franchise universe that defines modern sci-fi. Before all of that, there was Bali 2002, the harrowing miniseries about the Bali bombings that earned him serious dramatic credibility in Australia.

From Western Sydney to the Red Carpet

Heuston grew up in Baulkham Hills, in Sydney's western suburbs — a part of the city with a significant South Asian population, including one of Australia's largest Sri Lankan communities. His Sri Lankan heritage, rarely foregrounded in entertainment press, is confirmed by multiple Australian media profiles. He was scouted as a model while bartending during his first year at Macquarie University, and within a few years was walking for Fendi, Gucci, Louis Vuitton, and Burberry. The acting came later, almost by accident, after he appeared in a music video and "fell in love" with performing.

What Makes Off Campus Matter

Adapted from Elle Kennedy's enormously popular four-book Off Campus series, the show follows an elite college ice hockey team and the women orbiting their world — fake-dating tropes, consent conversations, and enough emotional whiplash to satisfy the BookTok audience that made the novels bestsellers. Critics have been largely kind. The Wrap called it "endearing and smart," while Screen Rant praised it as "surprisingly insightful." Prime Video renewed it for a second season before the first episode even aired — a sign of serious confidence.

Heuston's Justin Kohl is the character who diverges most from the book version. Originally written as a pure jock archetype, the series reimagines him as a music-obsessed introvert navigating identity and ambition alongside his romantic storyline. In a Collider interview, Heuston described the ending of his arc as something "we never saw coming," teasing future developments for Season 2.

The Diaspora Angle NRIs Should Notice

Here's why this matters beyond the romance bubble: South Asian representation in mainstream Western streaming shows remains painfully thin, and when it exists, it's almost always limited to explicitly "South Asian stories." Heuston's casting is different. He's playing a character whose ethnicity isn't the storyline — a universally appealing role in a show designed for global audiences. That kind of normalised representation is exactly what advocacy groups have been pushing for.

For NRI families in the US, UK, and Australia, Off Campus is streaming now on Prime Video — no geo-restrictions, no waiting for an international window. And if you've got a teenager who devoured the books, this is one of those rare adaptations that the reviews suggest actually works.

What's Next for Heuston

With Heartbreak High concluded after three seasons, Dune: Prophecy continuing on HBO, and Off Campus locked in for Season 2, Heuston is quietly building one of the most diverse filmographies of any young actor in the streaming era. The Sri Lankan-Australian kid from Baulkham Hills is having his moment — and the diaspora should be paying attention.
nri_angle: Josh Heuston is one of the rare South Asian-descent actors cast in a major Western streaming show where his ethnicity isn't the storyline — the kind of normalised representation NRIs have long advocated for. Off Campus streams globally on Prime Video with no geo-restrictions.
